sources.entry: FlowPeek - Previews the Mermaid diagram already on screen, read from a selection, the clipboard, the block under the pointer, or a file.

summary.one_liner: FlowPeek is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar app that draws Mermaid diagrams it finds on screen (under the pointer, in a selection, on the clipboard, or in a file) without sending anything off the Mac.
summary.what_it_does: It is a menu-bar app that finds Mermaid source in what is on screen and draws it. You can hold Option and point at a block, copy it to the clipboard, or select it, and it renders the diagram. It also outlines Mermaid blocks printed in Terminal, iTerm2 and Ghostty, including full-screen programs in Ghostty, and reads the caret position in VS Code and the plugin-based integration for Sublime Text. A Quick Look extension previews .mmd and .mermaid files in Finder, and double-clicking one opens a read-only preview window. Every diagram it draws is kept on a searchable "shelf" with a text search and a fallback meaning-based search that runs on the Mac. Drawn diagrams can be zoomed, panned, copied as an image, or saved as PNG, PDF or SVG. An optional AI feature, off by default, can write Mermaid from a description using a provider key the user supplies.
use_cases: preview a Mermaid diagram in a pull request or docs page
see the diagram a coding agent printed in the terminal
render Mermaid text copied to the clipboard
preview .mmd files in Finder with Quick Look
find and reopen a previously drawn diagram
export a Mermaid diagram as SVG, PNG or PDF
how_to_run: Or download the notarized disk image from the latest release
Grant Accessibility permission on first launch
Hold Option and point at a Mermaid block, then press Space
Or copy or select Mermaid text and use the badge or button that appears
Build from source: xcodebuild -project FlowPeek.xcodeproj -scheme FlowPeek -derivedDataPath /private/tmp/flowpeek-derived build
notable: Reads diagrams already on screen, including ones a coding agent printed into a terminal, with no file written to disk
Renders offline with bundled Mermaid under a strict CSP; no network request when drawing
Ghostty support asks the terminal for its grid size with a read-only ioctl to handle full-screen programs
VS Code and Sublime Text need setup steps (an accessibility setting or an optional plugin) to expose text
Only Accessibility permission is requested; no Screen Recording or Input Monitoring
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and the Accessibility permission for most gestures; copying works without it
VS Code needs Screen Reader Accessibility Mode or editor.accessibilitySupport set to on; Sublime Text needs an optional plugin
Terminal apps that paint text on a canvas, such as VS Code's integrated terminal, expose no text and cannot be read
The AI feature needs the user's own provider account and key, and is off until enabled
Distribution is outside the Mac App Store because App Sandbox is disabled
